correctness.rationale: All claims about the two committed 8x8 arrays were replayed independently. Latin property holds for K1,K2. Ordered K3,3-pattern test (Prop.1 of Krotov-Krotov) gives 0 hits on both; independent re-check with distinct-letter (induced) filter also gives 0 hits, so K3,3-freeness holds under both loose and strict readings. Exhaustive enumeration over all 8!=40320 column permutations gives T1=64 and T2=192, reproduced by verifier and by independent brute-force script. Maximum disjoint-transversal numbers p1=p2=8 are proved by exhibition: each listed 8-family partitions all 64 cells, each 8-set verified to contain all rows, columns and symbols (hence a transversal). Since 8 is the absolute upper bound at order 8, maximality is immediate with no UNSAT log needed. Mate squares from DRAFT were checked Latin and orthogonal (64 distinct ordered pairs) and each mate-symbol class verified a transversal, so mate existence follows via the standard mate-iff-partition theorem. Completeness of the class (exactly two members, unique nonempty case in orders 3-11) is explicitly relied upon from Brouwer-Wanless/Krotov-Krotov, not re-proved, and is disclosed as a limitation. This is proof by exhaustive deterministic enumeration (stdlib-only replay), not heuristic or sampled evidence.

originality.rationale: Substantive gap verified against nearest sources, not by timestamp. Krotov-Krotov arXiv:2304.07157 (v3, accepted Discrete Math 350 (2027) 115402) establishes the scope (no K3,3-free squares orders 3-7,9-11, exactly two at order 8 up to equivalence, order-16 switched construction, rectangle counts) but contains no transversal counts, disjoint-packing numbers, or mate verdicts for the two Figure-1 representatives — verified via full-text (ar5iv) inspection: transversals appear only as trade/eigenfunction motivation (Secs 2.1-2.2, Props 1-3) and Sec 5 discusses K4,4-freeness of MOLS, not packing/mate status of the order-8 pair. Cavenagh-Wanless arXiv:1609.03001 proves generic even-order transversal-free existence/abundance, saying nothing about these pattern-free members. Wanless survey arXiv:0903.5142 and Montgomery survey arXiv:2406.19873 cover existence/enumeration/generalisations but record no table for the K3,3-free order-8 pair. Kazemi-Pahlavsay arXiv:1808.05213 and Dennunzio et al. establish mate-iff-partition-into-N-disjoint-transversals, confirming mate status is a nontrivial decomposition claim not implied by single-transversal existence. No inspected source states T=64/192, p=8/8, or mate existence for these squares; the route (counting plus packing plus decomposition search over a pattern-avoidance class) differs from prior single-transversal censuses (SCOPE-FAIL-034 group-based 7-8 tau/N, SCOPE-FAIL-009 order-10 DCLS spectrum).

value.rationale: Independently worth finding: decides a recognized question at a natural classification boundary. The scope is the complete 2-member K3,3-free (universally-noncommutative-loop) class, uniquely nonempty at order 8 in 3-11, so order 8 is forced by the boundary, not an arbitrary slice. The target (maximum disjoint transversals / orthogonal-mate partition, Brualdi-Stein-Ryser direction described as most famous open problem in Kazemi-Pahlavsay) crossed with the Brouwer-Wanless/Krotov avoidance program has significance before computation: whether universal noncommutativity forces orthogonality failure. The outcome is informative either way; here both members admit mates (p=8) while transversal counts separate them (64 vs 192), so avoidance does not force orthogonality failure — a citable negative answer plus first packing data for the class. Not database repackaging (isotopy catalogues contain no transversal/packing/decomposition data), not a parameter substitution or tiny unmotivated gain, and not an unexplained enumeration: explicit partitions, mates, and certificates are given with mechanism interpretation.
